scope: Five existing NPC histories: Strange Talon, Captain Hildethrax, Ambassador Sophina, Guardian Commander Yvette and Kumai-218; one connected Ghilsen death account.

before.title: Commander Yvette
before.summary: A commander whose lifetime of service, wary dealings with visitors and grief for her soldiers give her corps a history of its own.

after.title: Commander Yvette
after.summary: A Guardian commander proud of a lifetime guarding Prima’s sacred ward. Her port is robbed, her corps remembers its dead, and later testimony about her own murder leaves a discrepancy the surviving scenes do not resolve.

after.personality: Observant, proud and capable of bargaining, contemplation and abrupt violence. His accusation against adventurers widens beyond named offenders; his later version of Swift’s attack leaves out words retained in the direct scene.
after.achievements: Receives embassy visitors, offers payment for strategically useful knowledge, watches Rahu access and receives Melian in custody after Magnus’s operation. Kills Swift Foot and wins the fatal duel with Ghilsen. Receiving a captive does not prove that he ordered every act of the kidnapping.
after.relationships: Ephraith is his sovereign; Sophina turns Rahu grievances into formal diplomatic demands. Hildethrax cooperates in access and investigation. Scribonia offers valuable knowledge, Olokun tests his patience, Magnus encounters his scars and hostility, and Cecil shares a brief contemplative conversation before duty interrupts.

after.personality: Proud, exact about hierarchy and capable of both patient explanation and abrupt dismissal. He defends the Rahu’s account of merit and acknowledges their commercial interests. He can call a former enemy a traitor and still honor the escort’s promise of safety.
after.achievements: Reports evidence in the Edran investigation, receives embassy visitors, guards access to archives, offers investigative cooperation, checks invitations and coordinates food and infrastructure negotiations. Later conducts the peace company along the overnight approach to the Queen. His stated second rank does not establish that he is second-in-command of the whole Rahu.
after.relationships: Ephraith exercises sovereignty; Sophina delegates practical follow-up; Talon supplies intelligence and a grievance Hildethrax takes seriously. Nienna’s exoneration remains the outcome of the earlier case. Olokun repeatedly presses his boundaries, while Anky’s prayer for both sides receives his permission during the peace approach.

after.personality: Composed, selective and capable of courtesy, condescension and severe judgment. She respects Lionel’s refusal of bloodshed without surrendering her own jurisdictional claim, and allows a useful outsider to approach without admitting him to state secrets.
after.achievements: Represents the Rahu at the council, presents the case concerning Talon, offers food sales, entrusts implementation to Hildethrax and conducts state negotiations with a retinue that includes treasurers. Lionel receives respect for a conviction she does not share.

after.personality: Direct, proud of her corps and wounded by the thought that divine newcomers could replace its lifetime of service. She tries to restore order after the stolen keys, defends the soldiers’ loyalty and remembers their graves. A narrated difficulty with deception is a scene observation, not a universal guarantee that she cannot lie.
after.achievements: Commands a corps at a private military port, coordinates loading and guards access to supplies and a sacred ward. Attempts to stop the theft and later offers to show the soldiers’ graves. A later hearing calls her a murder victim, while an intervening quest gives her dialogue; no complete death or return account is established.
after.relationships: Her soldiers are the people she calls loyal and continues to mourn. Navi questions her calling, Sparrow becomes the target of her detention order, and the escaping party defeats her control of the port. Farkur later confesses to enabling the escape, while Horgrith and Moliena keep the institutional grievance alive.

after.personality: Severe, observant and impatient with speeches. He can mock John’s restraint, appreciate it, call for refreshments and praise a solution in a few plain words. His judgments are forceful and remain open to disagreement.
after.achievements: Keeps the old arena, tests early arrivals, calls a Rahu war council, participates in the later vanguard contest and sets a field task that the company completes. Neither the arena’s safeguards nor his own account of divine assistance is generalized beyond its source context.
after.relationships: Melian brings early candidates, Quake earns his tactical respect and John challenges the cost of his training. Severina, Kasiri, Camilla, Thorn and their companions meet his later tests. The field task ends with Severina giving Moira credit, which Kumai acknowledges without his usual sharp reply.

editorialLimits: The owner requests NPCs next. Five existing NPC identities gain histories; Ghilsen receives one necessary connected account while remaining a player. No new person, page, asset, event or quotation is created.

Explicit owner canon and established quest narration/outcomes govern. Claims, professional judgments, hypothetical tests and retrospective accusations retain their speakers. An institutional title does not imply omniscience, unrestricted jurisdiction or hidden approval of every operation.

All 233 cited versions match two read-only corpora: 199 original main-quest export versions and 34 native API cache versions. Original payload timestamps remain exact. Discovery and large working windows do not imply exhaustive reading; unchanged earlier dossier/RP material retains its qualifications.

Talon Paran and Talon Procoyon are excluded from the Strange Talon selection; a shared name fragment does not establish identity. The native fatal Swift Foot thread is distinct from the main-channel follow-up and from the Aravil/Ithilrûnë allegations.

Swift attacks first with a stated intent to wound, discards his sword and speaks before Talon kills him. The direct words and narrator outcome take precedence over Talon’s abbreviated later account. Talon’s real injury and the attack do not erase the witnessed killing or the servants’ burial response. The later council charges remain a separate grievance.

The primary June duel narrator explicitly leaves Ghilsen’s corpse and Talon alive. This resolves that encounter’s outcome without inventing a full exchange of attacks, deciding Talon’s later fate or merging Ghilsen’s later revival with a separate later report of death.

Hildethrax’s second rank is not expanded into second-in-command. His account of merit and free choice remains a claim beside the costs he describes. His overnight escort, permission for prayer and referral to Hoshi identify his work without giving him the Queen’s negotiating authority or disclosing private rites.

Sophina’s limited hints, retinue and later public nod do not expose state negotiations, identify concealed figures, establish universal trust in Magnus or settle covert responsibility. Her original office remains ambassador rather than royalty. The January 2026 posting is a later public appearance, not an invented date for a political settlement.

Yvette’s port theft, later speaking scene and subsequent named murder report are preserved together. The source does not supply a death/return scene, establish a mistaken speaker name or reconcile the dates. An optional owner clarification is requested; absent a canon decision the discrepancy stays explicit. Her corps is not silently made the Pristinia militia.

Kumai’s arena safeguards remain bounded to the exercise. His claim that he or Namo’o awakened the field-test opponents is not independently witnessed. Trainees’ objections and the completed task coexist; praise does not manufacture agreement with his methods or a universal resurrection rule.

All 391 timeline objects, dates, importance, participants and region assignments remain exact. A two-paragraph council passage moves intact within Talon’s history for reading order. All 41 older section IDs/titles/evidence objects, every older source/link and all unrelated content/media/roles/maps/quotes/261 previews survive.

Raw/controller data, private origins, ritual procedures, concealed identities, private guide/mentor material, numerical rules/reward tables and unreviewed media remain external. Metadata contains only already-public editorial descriptions and source IDs/timestamps/hashes.
verification: PASS five complete NPC histories and connected Ghilsen account; 127 narrative paragraphs; 30 chapters; 41 old bookmarks; every evidence panel/reference/fact and original decoded portraits; saved reload/focus; fresh390/320 fit/header clearance; five NPC-directory/modal/profile journeys; eight connected links and three searches; separate Talon grievances and explicit Yvette discrepancy; unchanged roles/roster/public-private boundaries; no script/public HTTP errors. Source/preservation, canonical, calendar, portrait, protected-asset, browse-preview, syntax and whitespace checks pass; representative local screenshots are inspected.
